title: function-calling parse debug scratchpad
content:
Goal: capture investigation steps and hypotheses for recurring parse failures when using function/tool calling (chat completion + structured output) from hosted API. Notes to self and breadcrumbs for whoever picks this up.

Summary of issue:
- Intermittent failures where the assistant returns a JSON blob that fails our downstream schema validation for the tool call.
- Failure modes: trailing commas, unescaped newlines in string fields, top-level non-object (assistant returned an array), or valid JSON but wrong shape (missing required key `items`).
- Appears more frequent when response is streamed and when messages are longer / include code blocks.

Repro commands tried locally (node/python snippets paraphrased):
- curl POST to /v1/chat/completions with function schema: {"name":"save_metadata","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"id":{"type":"string"},"items":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object"}}},"required":["id","items"]}}
- SDK: redwood.chat.create({model, messages, functions: [schema], function_call: 'auto'}) -> then parse assistant.function_call.arguments as JSON.parse()
- Streaming test: open websocket + stream chunks to client, assemble, then parse at end

Sample failing assistant outputs (copied raw):
1) Truncated / streaming boundary issue:
   "{"id":"abc-123", "items": [ {"name": "foo", "value": "bar"},"  <-- missing closing ]}"
   JSON.parse throws: "SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input"

2) Trailing comma (assistant injected list with comment):
   {"id":"abc-123", "items": [{"name":"x", "value": 1},],}
   JSON.parse fails with: "SyntaxError: Unexpected token '}'"

3) Assistant returned text wrapper (not pure JSON):
   "Here's the result:\n\n{\n  \"id\": \"abc-123\",\n  \"items\": []\n}"
   -> Our parser (expecting strict JSON) chokes unless we strip leading text and use first brace match.

4) Unescaped newline inside string field:
   {"id":"abc-123", "items": [{"name":"note", "value":"line1
line2"}]}
   -> JSON.parse is fine for properly escaped, but sometimes assistant returns literal newline in the chunk which breaks parse when assembling.

Hypotheses:
- Streaming + chunk boundaries sometimes split mid-escape sequence (e.g., "\n" becomes actual newline during concatenation) when client assembly code doesn't preserve byte/char boundaries correctly.
- The model sometimes outputs explanatory text around the JSON. When function_call is used, spec says assistant should output arguments only, but we still see wrapper text occasionally (race with system prompts or older model behavior).
- When the model is switching between tool-call vs normal text due to ambiguous prompt, it may output non-object like an array.
- Prompt or examples in system messages that include trailing commas or human-written pseudo-JSON may bias model to include them.

What I've tried and results:
- Strict parsing after stripping everything before first '{' and after last '}'. This reduced noise but introduced risk (could grab unrelated JSON inside explanation).
- Robust incremental parser using a stack counter (count { and }) to detect balanced top-level object across streaming chunks. This works well for objects but fails when assistant wraps with text before/after braces. I added heuristic to find first '{' weight, then parse until balanced. Edge case: arrays at top-level (we expect object).
- Regex fallback to try to match first JSON object: /\{(?:[^{}]|(?R))*\}/ (JS doesn't support (?R) so implemented manual scanner).
- Post-parse schema validation using AJV to catch missing keys. AJV errors: missing property 'items' in ~30% of failing cases.
- Forced function_call: 'name' in request (server side) to ensure the assistant uses the function call channel instead of free text. This reduced frequency a lot but not fully (still see 2-3/week).

Notes on streaming assembly (current implementation):
- We buffer chunks as strings. We have tests where chunk 1 ends with "...\\" and chunk 2 starts with "n" which turns a literal escape into actual newline. That explains some unescaped newline cases.
- Switching to binary-safe concatenation (Buffer concat in node) and decode at the end with utf8 seems to have reduced character-escape corruption. Need to verify across different client languages.

Open actions / TODOs:
- [ ] Add robust streaming tests that simulate escape-splitting across boundaries (unit tests with chunk splits at random positions).
- [ ] Add server-side enforcement: request param function_call: {name: 'save_metadata'} to force function channel when applicable (done in staging for a subset). Monitor anomaly rate.
- [ ] Improve parser heuristics: prefer balanced object from first '{' but also verify that parsed JSON matches schema before accepting. If not, continue scanning for next balanced object (limit scans to first 5 candidates).
- [ ] Add a warning metric whenever regex/heuristic parsing is used (to track how often assistant returns wrapped text).
- [ ] File a model prompt tweak: tighten system and user examples showing exact expected output (explicitly: JSON only, no explanatory text). Put PR link in linked_artifacts.
- [ ] Run local fuzzing where we sample model responses (few-shot) to try to reproduce trailing comma and array-top-level cases.

Questions / decisions for eng leads:
- Do we accept heuristic parsing in the SDK (but surface an explicit warning) or enforce hard-fail and surface parsing failure to customers? My leaning: prefer safe hard-fail by default, but allow an opt-in tolerant mode for internal teams.

Quick reproduction steps for reviewer:
1) Use the staging API key: POST /v1/chat/completions with functions schema included and function_call: 'auto' or omitted to reproduce higher error rate.
2) Use the streaming endpoint and split the response into random chunk sizes (library: curl --http2 --no-buffer + simulate partial frames).
3) Observe parse failures in the SDK logs (tag: func-parse-fail).

Breadcrumbs for future debugging:
- Related GH PR: redwood-sdk/#412 (see linked artifacts) for earlier fix to streaming buffer.
- SRE: alert channel #ingest-tooling maybe noisy, mute for this test.
- Keep an eye on ERRORS metric: function_call_parse_error.rate (Grafana dashboard: /d/parse-errors)

Notes to self: document final tolerant-vs-strict behavior in SDK README and platform docs (console: per-customer setting?). Pull in Priya for design review on error surfaceability.

End of scratchpad.
